title: Sorting, Searching & Common Patterns
intro: Sorting and searching interview questions for Python freshers come up in two forms: theory questions ('explain bubble sort and its time complexity') and live coding questions ('find duplicates in a list'). This page covers bubble sort and insertion sort (the two sorts you must be able to code from memory and explain), the built-in sort() and sorted() with key functions (the Python way that you'd use in production), linear search and binary search (with the precondition for binary search — the list must be sorted — which is the first follow-up every interviewer asks), and the two simple problem-solving patterns that solve most fresher coding rounds: two pointers for sorted-array problems and the frequency-count pattern using a dict for string/array duplication problems. Each pattern comes with a worked example in 10–15 lines of runnable Python.
